subject.title: RFC: Readiness Conditions and Standard Hosting Profiles

question: Should OpenClaw initially accept a staged canonical readiness foundation, or commit now to the full plugin-provider, hosting-profile, CLI, artifact-identity, and release-conformance contract?
rationale: The implementation demonstrates feasibility, but only maintainers can choose the permanent availability, plugin API, configuration, upgrade, and support obligations.

options.title: Accept a staged foundation
options.body: Approve canonical core conditions and legacy-compatible projections first, then require separate acceptance for broader provider, profile, CLI, artifact, and release surfaces.

options.title: Accept the full contract
options.body: Approve every proposed public surface and explicitly own its compatibility and packaged release-test obligations.

options.title: Keep composition external
options.body: Retain fixed Gateway readiness and leave supplemental hosting checks to hosts or plugins.

recommendation.title: Accept a staged foundation
recommendation.body: Approve canonical core conditions and legacy-compatible projections first, then require separate acceptance for broader provider, profile, CLI, artifact, and release surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history provides the strongest cross-cutting ownership signal for the Gateway and runtime contracts this RFC would standardize.
